questions.q: With no mapping configured, how does the Copy activity map source data to sink?
options: By column position (ordinal) only
By column name, case-sensitively
It refuses to run without explicit mapping
By data type, ignoring column names entirely
questions.explain: Default mapping matches source and sink columns by name. If the sink doesn't exist yet, the source's names simply become the sink's.

questions.q: What does "schema drift" mean in this context?
options: A pipeline gradually running slower over time
A sink table being deleted unexpectedly
A dataset losing its linked service reference
Source columns changing between pipeline runs, which default mapping can absorb automatically
questions.explain: Schema drift describes source columns changing from run to run — a new column added, say. Default, by-name mapping picks up whatever the source returns each time, with no pipeline change required.

questions.q: When would you reach for explicit mapping instead of default mapping?
options: Only for Copy activities using a self-hosted integration runtime
To copy only part of the source data, rename columns, or reshape data between structures
Explicit mapping is never actually necessary
Only when copying between two identical schemas
questions.explain: Explicit mapping handles subsetting columns, renaming them, and reshaping hierarchical data into a tabular sink — none of which default mapping can do.

questions.q: How do you map columns from a source file that has no header row?
options: By ordinal (column position), since there are no column names to match against
It's impossible to copy a file with no header row
The Copy activity generates random column names automatically
By column name, exactly like any other source
questions.explain: With no header row, there's nothing for default by-name mapping to match against — explicit mapping by ordinal (position) is required instead.

questions.q: What does Collection reference do when mapping a hierarchical source to a tabular sink?
options: Converts the entire source into a single JSON blob column
Deletes the array field entirely from the output
Only applies to SQL Server sources, never to JSON or MongoDB
Selects the array to iterate over, cross-applying it so one nested object becomes multiple flat rows
questions.explain: Collection reference tells the mapping which array to flatten — the service cross-applies it against the object's other fields to produce multiple tabular rows.
